name: figure
title: Figure
description: One picture a document holds, a chart, a diagram, a photograph or a screenshot, with the page and the box it sits in, and a chart's values when they were read.

files.api/service.yaml:
# THE FIGURE'S FUNCTIONS (docs/unoverse/data/objects/README.md 4b). A figure of a document (ruled
# 2026-09-11) shows the picture kept at read time, or is rendered from its page on request,
# the region its box names, on the platform's own document service: nothing is stored, and the
# picture goes to the screen, never into a model's context. A chart whose values a vision read
# found (docs/unoverse/data/documents/review.md) returns them as rows beside its picture.
getDetail:
  description: The figure's picture, kept at read time or rendered from its page and box, and a chart's values as rows.
  calls:
    # THE PICTURE KEPT AT READ TIME: a link to it, and the browser loads it.
    - name: stored
      node: S3FileContent
      when: "return !!row.content.pictureKey"
      config:
        bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
        key: "{{ row.content.pictureKey }}"
        includeContent: false
    # Drawn from the page only for a figure read before pictures were kept.
    - name: file
      node: S3FileContent
      when: "return !calls.stored && !!row.content.partId && !!row.content.key && !!row.content.page"
      config:
        bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
        key: "{{ row.content.key }}"
        includeContent: false
    - name: picture
      node: RenderDocument
      when: "return !calls.stored && !!row.content.partId && !!row.content.key && !!row.content.page"
      config:
        fileUrl: "{{ calls.file.file.downloadUrl }}"
        fileName: "return String(row.content.key).split('/').at(-1)"
        page: "{{ row.content.page }}"
        box: "return row.content.box ? JSON.stringify(row.content.box) : ''"
        dpi: 150
    - name: rows
      node: S3FileContent
      when: "return !!row.content.rowsKey"
      config:
        bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
        key: "{{ row.content.rowsKey }}"
        includeContent: true
  returns: >-
    return (() => {
      const t = calls.rows && calls.rows.file && calls.rows.file.content ? JSON.parse(calls.rows.file.content) : null;
      const rows = t && Array.isArray(t.rows) ? t.rows : [];
      const image = calls.stored && calls.stored.file ? { url: calls.stored.file.downloadUrl, mimeType: 'image/png' } : calls.picture ? calls.picture.image : null;
      return Object.assign({}, image ? { image: image } : {},
        rows.length ? { header: t.header || [], rows: rows, total: rows.length, matched: rows.length } : {});
    })()
files.figure.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
type: object
name: figure
element: content
icon: chart-column
meta: open

# A PICTURE A DOCUMENT HOLDS (owner, 2026-09-14: "when we extract images inside a document, we
# should call it something else"): a chart, a diagram, a photograph or a screenshot taken from a
# document, made as a part of it (`partsOf`), off the map like a table. Walked to from its
# document and never searched: it declares no `embed`. A picture the business publishes is an
# `image`, on the map.

title: Figure
description: >-
  One picture a document holds, a chart, a diagram, a photograph or a screenshot, with the page
  and the box it sits in, and a chart's values when they were read.
whenToUse: >-
  See or read a picture from a document: a performance chart, an exposure breakdown, an
  organisation chart, a process diagram. Open it from the document it is part of; a chart whose
  values were read also answers with them as rows.
category: Objects
version: 1.0.0

props: { $include: props }
files.props.yaml:
# A FIGURE'S FIELDS. Every one is written from the parse by the pipeline, never by the model
# (input: false): the document's make function shapes each figure once, and the part writer keeps
# the fields by name (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/README.md layer 1, parts).
universal_id:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The row's permanent handle, minted from the document's id and the figure's own, so a re-read finds the same row.
title:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The figure's caption, or what it shows and where it sits.
description:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: One line on what the figure shows, so a walk can choose without opening it.
org:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The organisation whose row this is. Assigned by the run.
source_url:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The file the figure sits in, the same address as its document.
source_id:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The file's source id, the same as its document's.
kind:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: What the picture is, from the figure classifier. Chart, diagram, flowchart, photograph or screenshot.
partId:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The figure's id within its document's structure, such as f12.
page:
  type: number
  input: false
  description: The page the figure sits on, counted from 1.
box:
  type: object
  input: false
  description: Where on the page the figure sits, in points with the origin top-left, as x0, y0, x1, y1.
bucket:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The bucket the document sits in.
key:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The document's key in the bucket; the figure is drawn from its page when no picture was kept.
whenToUse:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The question this part answers, as its document's read named it, so a walk can choose it without opening it.
rowsKey:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: For a chart whose values were read into rows, the key of those rows in the store, under the document's folder in `_parsed/`, which its detail reads.
checks:
  type: object
  input: false
  description: For a chart whose values were read into rows, how they were read and why to check a value against the picture (docs/unoverse/data/documents/checks.md).
pictureKey:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The key of the picture kept at read time, under the document's folder in `_parsed/`, which its detail shows from S3.
